name: swift_audio_workstation
description: Embedded Swift audio workstation example that sequences and mixes kick, hi-hat, and synthesized bass into a six-second Float32 buffer.

imports.name: encode
imports.description: Receives the context, linear-memory address, and byte length of the completed Float32 audio buffer.

tests.description: sequence and mix six seconds of kick, hi-hat, and bass audio

steps.description: synthesize 264,600 Float32 samples and submit the buffer
check the waveform half a second into the sequence
check the waveform one second into the sequence

tests.notes: The callback proves the full six-second buffer length, while three separated waveform windows verify deterministic synthesis and changing sequencer/mixer state rather than a zero-filled or repeated buffer.

source.description: AudioWorkstation Mix example from Swift's Apache-2.0 with Runtime Library Exception WebAssembly examples, including MIT-licensed Vult DSP sources.

toolchain.name: Swift Embedded WebAssembly toolchain + Binaryen
toolchain.command: swift build --disable-sandbox --triple wasm32-unknown-none-wasm -c release --product Mix -Xcc -U__wasm_bulk_memory__; cp .build/wasm32-unknown-none-wasm/release/Mix.wasm stage/swift_audio_workstation.wasm; ./scripts/prepare

notes: The Swift application sources are Apache-2.0 with the Swift Runtime Library Exception. Vendored Vult DSP sources are MIT-licensed, and the remaining vendored allocator/libc sources carry permissive CC0, MIT, or Apache-2.0 with LLVM exception terms documented upstream. The official Swift 6.2 macOS package used for the clean build has SHA-256 9eac4a13500c7a6dedfd90814fd31c17af2efc38150137b56b70bf5f44b2d64b. Tests call the raw Wasm export and inspect its memory directly without the browser demo host.
